findings: The November 7, 2026 capture adds a two-link index at the PAYCO South Korea acceptance URL (new raw 1–12). The matched May 8, 2026 capture documents those two variants (old raw 1–8 and 105–107). Diff line 300 joins the prior final sentence and first new link. Compare the preserved originals at old raw 296–298 and new raw 11–12.

The dated Checkout guidance describes 28 merchant locations including Singapore, South Korean buyers, KRW presentment and all line items, and Checkout payment mode with setup and subscription mode unavailable. Dynamic presentation and manual selection are alternative Checkout configurations. Keep the 100 KRW minimum, no card-passthrough maximum and separate 2,000,000 KRW stored-value top-up ceiling (old raw 10–46). The separate Direct API creates and confirms a PaymentIntent using server-supplied client secret and browser confirmation (old raw 115–149 and 218–276).

The mapped summary retains the basic routes but overgeneralizes the sample omissions, leaves the NICEPAY disclosure scope and test/outcome transitions unclear, and omits the visible browser error-reference discrepancy (source 13–36; old raw 128–145 and 218–286).
historical_claims_to_preserve: Keep May 8, 2026 Checkout prerequisites and limits dated. The hosted example uses `success_url`, and the full embedded example instead uses `return_url` and `ui_mode: embedded_page` (old raw 48–99). The May Korea overview independently lists PAYCO one-time support and no recurring support (raw/stripe-korea-payment-methods-2025.md:144-154). The general product list for the South Korean method family does not expand the PAYCO mode matrix.

Keep the dated Direct API Stripe account prerequisite and PaymentIntent amount, `krw`, `payco` type, server-to-client secret handoff, and browser `stripe.confirmPayment` with `return_url`. The May Direct API section explicitly requires the merchant page to show the NICEPAY disclosure and terms link (old raw 115–149 and 218–269).

Keep local processor authentication and authorization, browser return with the PaymentIntent ID and client secret for status verification, and paid status as separate steps. In the dated test redirects, `requires_action` becomes `succeeded` on test authorization or `requires_payment_method` on test failure. Optional post-payment handling uses `payment_intent.succeeded` through Dashboard, webhook or partner integration (old raw 101–103 and 271–298).
conflicts: Source lines 13 and 21 and Korea concept line 66 assert that buyer email and a funding field are unnecessary. Old raw 128–145 and 243–269 omit these inputs in the illustrated PAYCO requests. The May Naver Direct API guide supplies an optional card/points funding setting (raw/stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:134-158), and the May Kakao payment guide explicitly requires email within Direct API (raw/stripe-kakao-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:135-139). Keep those method-specific descriptions and avoid inferring a universal PAYCO request rule or general integration complexity from sample omissions.

The explicit merchant-page NICEPAY instruction and link belong to the dated Direct API client section (old raw 218–222). Source line 22 and Korea concept line 67 should scope that requirement and avoid implying identical implementation in every Korean UI or method.

Source lines 28–36 leave the verified outcome implicit. Old raw 271–298 distinguishes browser return and verified status, and lists multiple ways to handle the success event. The May code destructures `error` at 252, then uses `result.error.message` at 266 without a shown `result` binding. Flag the dated example issue when routing to the code.

source_assessments.reason: The November raw provides navigation. The baseline summary independently requires scope and status corrections that affect how a reader selects a route, completes checkout and interprets the payment result.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payco/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-12 identify PAYCO acceptance in South Korea and link Checkout and Direct API. The detailed May 8, 2026 capture describes South Korean customers, 28 merchant locations including Singapore, KRW line items, Checkout payment mode only, and a 100 KRW minimum. It distinguishes the 2,000,000 KRW stored-value top-up cap from card passthrough, and dynamic presentation from manual `payco` enablement (old raw lines 10-46). Direct API uses a server-created KRW PaymentIntent, then browser `stripe.confirmPayment` with its client secret and `return_url`. The merchant page shows the dated NICEPAY disclosure and terms link. The buyer authenticates with the local processor, returns to the merchant, and the merchant verifies PaymentIntent status. Sandbox authorization and failure lead to `succeeded` and `requires_payment_method` respectively (old raw lines 128-149 and 218-298). source-stripe-payco-accept-payment.md retains the basic routes but needs these scope and outcome qualifications and more precise treatment of buyer email and funding examples.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payco/accept-a-payment, new raw lines 5-12 are navigation only to the same routes represented in old raw lines 6-8 and 105-107. Keep the May Checkout eligibility, KRW, mode and amount conditions dated. The Stripe-hosted example uses `success_url` and the full embedded example uses `return_url` with `ui_mode: embedded_page` (old raw lines 20-99). In source-stripe-payco-accept-payment.md and the reciprocal Korea concept, PAYCO’s illustrated Direct API requests omit buyer email and a funding selector, while the separate Naver guide documents an optional card/points selector. This example comparison supplies no universal PAYCO field rule (old raw lines 128-145 and 243-269; raw/stripe-naver-pay-accept-payment-2025.md:134-158). Scope the explicit NICEPAY merchant-page text and terms link to Direct API, and keep local authorization, browser return, verified server payment state and settlement distinct. The archived JavaScript uses `result.error.message` after destructuring `error`; the test states and success event are separate from that sample code (old raw lines 218-298).
